subject.title: [Feature/RFC]: Add eval-backed option discovery to avoid premature convergence in route/strategy answers

question: Should OpenClaw make anti-premature-convergence option discovery a default invariant for route, strategy, or choice answers, and which default runtime pairs must satisfy it?
rationale: Current main has adjacent tool-discipline and Codex web-search plumbing but no explicit option-discovery contract, and changing default answer strategy affects cost, latency, prompt ownership, and runtime parity.

options.title: Approve eval-first default invariant
options.body: Accept the behavior direction only as a generic QA Lab scenario first, then require a narrow runtime/prompt contract after the eval shape is proven.

options.title: Route to opt-in research profile
options.body: Keep default agents lean and track this as an optional best-insight or research profile instead of a default OpenClaw behavior.

options.title: Defer pending deterministic repro
options.body: Leave the RFC open until maintainers or contributors provide a reproducible current-main eval that captures the failure without private incident data.

recommendation.title: Approve eval-first default invariant
recommendation.body: Accept the behavior direction only as a generic QA Lab scenario first, then require a narrow runtime/prompt contract after the eval shape is proven.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prompt-surface and Codex workspace-routing history is closest to the decision boundary for adding a scoped invariant without undoing harness separation.
